title: How to Avoid Running Out of Money in Retirement (Longevity Planning)
description: Strategies to ensure your assets outlast your lifespan, even if you live to 100.
content:
The greatest fear for most retirees is not death, but running out of money before death. This is called 'Longevity Risk.' With modern medicine extending lifespans, a 65-year-old couple has a 50% chance that at least one spouse will live to age 92. A plan designed to last until 85 might leave you destitute for the final decade of your life. To avoid this, you must shift from 'Probability-Based' planning (hoping the market returns 8%) to 'Safety-First' planning (guaranteeing income for life). This guide explains how to build a portfolio that can survive a century.

Key Takeaways

  • Guaranteed Income Floor: Cover your essential expenses (Food, Housing, Utilities) with guaranteed income sources like Social Security, Pensions, and Annuities. If the market crashes to zero, you still eat.
  • The 3.5% Rule: The standard 4% withdrawal rule has a 5-10% failure rate over 30 years. For a 40-year horizon (retiring early or living long), lowering your withdrawal rate to 3.5% drastically increases safety.
  • Deferred Income Annuities (QLAC): You can buy a 'longevity insurance' policy inside your IRA. You pay a lump sum at 65, and it starts paying a monthly check at age 85. It is cheap insurance against living too long.
  • Variable Spending: The ability to cut spending by 10-20% during a market crash is the single most effective way to preserve your portfolio. Flexibility prevents ruin.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Social Security is an inflation-adjusted annuity that you cannot outlive. Delaying your claim until age 70 maximizes this 'Longevity Insurance.' It provides a larger guaranteed base for your 90s than any private investment product.

The Longevity Portfolio

How to structure assets for a 100-year life.

1. The Inflation Hedge (Stocks)

Problem: Inflation. $50,000 today buys $25,000 worth of goods in 25 years.
Solution: You must hold 50-60% equities even in retirement. You need the growth to maintain purchasing power in your 80s.

2. The Tail Risk Hedge (QLAC)

Problem: Living to 105 and depleting assets.
Solution: Use $100k of IRA money to buy a QLAC. It pays $0 for 20 years, then kicks in at age 85 with a guaranteed check. It removes the stress of 'pacing' your withdrawals perfectly.

3. The Buffer Asset (Home Equity)

Problem: Running out of liquid cash at 90.
Solution: Maintain a paid-off home. If you deplete your portfolio, you can access a Reverse Mortgage (HECM) line of credit to fund your final years without moving.

Tactical Steps

  1. Delay Social Security to 70: This is non-negotiable for longevity planning. The 8% annual increase is actuarially fair if you die average age, but it is a massive 'win' if you live to 95.
  2. Invest in Health: The most expensive part of aging is frailty. Gym memberships and healthy food are financial investments. Compressing your 'morbidity' window saves millions.
  3. Automate the Floor: Ensure your fixed income covers your fixed costs. Do not rely on selling stocks to pay the electric bill.
  4. Annual Review: At age 75, check your withdrawal rate. If your portfolio has grown, you can spend more. If it has shrunk, cut back. Don't fly blind.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I die early?

Then you left money on the table. That is the 'cost' of insurance. Most people prefer 'dying with too much' over 'living with too little'.

Is 4% safe?

Historically yes, but with high valuations and low bond yields, many experts suggest 3.3% to 3.8% is the new 'Safe' rate for a 30+ year horizon.

Do I need Long Term Care insurance?

It helps. Living to 100 increases the probability of needing cognitive care. A policy ensures you don't drain the portfolio intended for your spouse.
